newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokesman Filippo di Robilant briefed on Thursday and Friday's Fisheries Council. He said discussions would focus on tax and quotas for 1997, satellite control measures and the multi-annual guidance programme. He also said there would be bilateral contacts on Thursday morning followed by a plenary session at 1500/1400 GMT and on Friday morning.

Spokesman Peter Guilford briefed on Monday's EU/U.S. summit. He said discussions in plenary session had focused on the progress of the Singapore WTO Ministerial including the Information Technology Agreement (ITA), on a mutual recognition agreement, on EU membership of the Korean Energy Development Organisation and on Chinese membership of the World Trade Organisation.

Guilford also briefed on Tuesday's EU/Canada summit in Ottawa. He said discussions had focused on extra-territoriality and on labour standards. He said an action plan and a joint declaration had been signed between the EU and Canada.
Spokesman Nicolaas Wegter said an agreement on steel had been reached between the EU and Poland. He said the Commission hoped it could be formalised by the Council in the coming days.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/1175: Second GSM operator in Spain: the Commission requests clarification from the Spanish authorities.
- IP/96/1178: Commission clears GBP 371 million aid for British coal sector.
- IP/96/1187: Commission adopts a new steel aid code for the years 1997-2002.
- IP/96/1190: Burma: Commission decides withdrawal of Generalised System of Preferences benefits.
- IP/96/1193: Commission takes position on farm aid in Sicily (Italy).
- IP/96/1194: Commission clears aid for shifting of egg production from battery cage to alternative systems in Denmark.
- IP/96/1195: Commission clears aid to Diano but refuses aid to four other Italian iron and steel enterprises.
- IP/96/1196: Forges de Clabecq: Commission finds the Region of Wallonia measures incompatible with the steel aid code.
- IP/96/1197: Commission decides to extend the Andreatta-Van Miert agreement for six months to ensure IRI debt reduction.
- IP/96/1198: Commission decides to maintain the current shipbuilding aid ceilings.
- IP/96/1199: Peat industry in Ireland: no aid involved in favour of Bord na Mona, says the Commission.
- IP/96/1200: Commission clears DM 662 million aid for research for new Laenders.
- IP/96/1201: Commission clears a DM 9 million soft loan by the Bavarian authorities with a view to restructuring ADIS.
- IP/96/1202: Commission approves the redefinition of regional aid areas in Germany for the period of 1997-1999.
- IP/96/1203: Commission approves regional aid to Ford Motor Company in support of an investment project in Bridgend, South Wales.
- IP/96/1204: Commission launches an investigation into Thomson SA and Thomson Multimedia.
- IP/96/1205: Commission launches investigation into DM 4.8 million state aid to Thueringer Motorenwerke GmbH.
- IP/96/1206: Commission grants ECU 750,000 for 50 young European voluntary doctors in the framework of the European programme for reconstruction and development in South Africa.
- IP/96/1207: Red Cross staff members killed in Chechnya: Commission strongly condemns this barbaric act.
- IP/96/1208: Commission clears Belgian high-speed train financing.
- IP/96/1209: Commissioner van den Broek welcomes release of Nikitin.
- IP/96/1121: Fighting tobacco consumption: Commission examines available options.
- Speech/96/335: Speech by Commissioner Edith Cresson on European electronic network for schools.
- Speech/96/336: Speech by Commissioner Neil Kinnock on EU seafarers.
- Memo/96/122: Commission and World Bank talks on evaluation.
- Communication to the Council and the European Parliament on the present and the proposed Community role in combating tobacco consumption.
